clue.text: Fletcher has designs on prison uniforms with Mackay innocently trusting him at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter, so only each word's front letter is kept

blocks.note: old British convict uniforms were printed with broad arrows
the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A scene from the prison sitcom Porridge, with old lag Fletcher scheming against warder Mr Mackay.
explanation.walkthrough: Fletcher and Mackay are the convict and the warder in the BBC prison sitcom Porridge, but here Fletcher is the definition. ARROWSMITH is the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher is a maker of arrows, which is exactly what an arrowsmith is: two trade names for the same craftsman.

clue.text: Invalid entrance to nightclub gets jammed, not opening

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so the word's front letter is the one kept
without its opening, a word loses the letter it starts with

blocks.note: first letter of the club
a jammed venue is packed full

explanation.surface: A doorman's complaint: the club is packed and nobody can get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a person who is ill, but it is the adjective, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Null, as in null and void, describes something with no legal force, a standard synonym for invalid.

clue.text: End sentence with period children are taught

blocks.note: a term is a limit or end point, as in the term of a contract
doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A teacher reminding pupils to finish each sentence with a full stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End sentence with period' reads like punctuation advice, but 'period' belongs to the definition and means a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Term-time is the part of the year when schools are in session, as opposed to the holidays.

clue.text: Definitely where Sir should go to be loved!

definitions.text: where Sir should go to be loved

blocks.note: first meaning: certainly, as an emphatic agreement

blocks.clueFragment: where Sir should go to be loved
blocks.note: second meaning, read as two words: placing SIR inside DEED makes DESIRED, a word for loved

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful cryptic hint: put SIR in DEED and you get DE-SIR-ED, so 'in deed' is where Sir goes to be desired.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic adverb used to confirm or strengthen a statement, meaning certainly or truly.

clue.text: French noblemen’s ‘à votre santé’, drinking a litre between six

indicators.note: one who drinks takes something inside, so the outer word swallows the rest
to sit between is to be flanked on both sides, so the parts placed there are surrounded

blocks.note: the French toast, 'to your health', in English is cheers
Roman numeral six
taken as written
standard abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: French aristocrats raising their glasses and sharing a litre of wine among six of them.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two nested containers: the litre sits inside the Roman six, and that whole unit goes inside the toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is a French title of nobility, the rank of knight, so chevaliers are French noblemen.

clue.text: Slowly run out of unopened alcohol

indicators.note: something unopened is missing its opening, so the front letter goes

blocks.note: booze is informal for alcohol

explanation.surface: A drinker whose supply slowly dwindles because the bottles stay sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out of' looks like a phrase about exhausting supplies, but 'of' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze is to seep or trickle out gradually, the way liquid leaks slowly through a gap.

clue.text: Players of games put on half-length legwear

indicators.note: cut to half its length, the word keeps only its first half

blocks.note: trousers are legwear
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: Sportsmen pulling on cropped shorts or knee-length trousers before a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players of games' wants to be the definition, but 'games' is wordplay: PE, school physical education. 'Put on' places it after the cut-down legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of actors or performers, and players is an old word for actors.

clue.text: Several gods - the acting god of nature to the fore

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild and of nature
taken as written
an actor who is on is performing

explanation.surface: Among several deities, the nature god takes the lead as acting head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the fore' tells you to move PAN to the front, ahead of THE and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the collective set of gods worshipped by one people, such as the Greek or Norse gods.

clue.text: Need peer to crush a Parisian uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top
to crush something is to squeeze it, so one word grips the other

blocks.note: to pry is to peer nosily
une is French for a

explanation.surface: A call for a nobleman to put down a revolt in Paris, as in the French Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord, but here it is a verb meaning to look nosily.
explanation.definitionFit: Penury is extreme poverty, a state of want, and need is a standard synonym for that condition.

clue.text: Fielding - possibly with new spinning stars

indicators.note: spinning round turns something about, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: the fielding side with new spin bowlers who are stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Fielding sounds like cricket, but it is Noel Fielding, the British comedian; 'possibly' marks him as one example of a Noel.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Fielding, of The Mighty Boosh and Great British Bake Off, is one person who bears the first name Noel.

clue.text: Worker works with skilful movements

blocks.note: a man is a worker, as in a hired man
oeuvres are an artist's works

explanation.surface: An employee who does the job deftly and with nimble motions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' sounds like a verb for the worker, but it is a noun: the French oeuvres, a body of works.
explanation.definitionFit: Manoeuvres are deft, carefully planned moves, as in steering a vehicle or outwitting an opponent.

clue.text: Trained pear lies against the wall?

definitions.text: Trained pear lies against the wall?

indicators.note: something trained has been shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's fruit tree, a pear trained flat to grow against the garden wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: as wordplay it rearranges two words, and read straight it describes the answer exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a fruit tree whose branches are trained flat along a wall or framework.

clue.text: Alt-Right advantage for Left-Bankers?

definitions.note: plural noun for a collective noun

indicators.note: short for alter, so the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political jibe: does the Alt-Right movement give the Left an edge?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alt-Right' and 'Left' suggest politics, but Alt is short for alter and the Left Bank is the bohemian artists' quarter of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The avant-garde are experimental artists, typified by the painters and writers of Paris's Left Bank.

clue.text: See 19
Night-time predator pursuing insect into willow

blocks.note: a cricket is a chirping insect
bats hunt at night

explanation.surface: A bat chasing an insect into the branches of a willow tree at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursuing' puts the predator after the insect. Willow looks like the tree, but it stands for what is made from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are traditionally made from willow wood, so willow is a common metonym for the bat.

clue.text: Incidents of motorway madness? They're insubstantial

definitions.note: a clause meaning things that are insubstantial

blocks.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with 1 read as I
rage is madness or fury
incidents means more than one, so the word is plural

explanation.surface: Road-rage outbursts on the motorway, dismissed as trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'motorway madness' as M1 RAGES: bouts of road rage on the M1, the London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirages are optical illusions with no real substance, things seen that are not actually there.

clue.text: Fatigue turning into bout of fever

indicators.note: turning into something else means changing form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tiredness developing into a feverish illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads naturally as a medical progression; 'turning into' is the signal that rearranges the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for malarial fever with shivering, so an ague-fit is one attack of it.

clue.text: Nothing trivial, perhaps, upset tribal leader

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down clue that turns the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: O looks like zero
minor means of little importance
e.g., for example, signals perhaps

explanation.surface: A chief who gets angry over something that is really no small matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces are joined first, then the whole string is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was a famous Apache war chief who resisted US forces in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Start a Ximenean section for A to Z connoisseurs?

indicators.note: a section is a cut-out part, so the letters come from a stretch of the text

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the third

explanation.surface: Advice to crossword lovers: begin with a Ximenean section, the strictly fair kind of puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ximenean refers to Ximenes, the setter whose rules define fair cryptic clueing. The A to Z is the classic London street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxi drivers must know every street, so they are experts on the routes listed in an A to Z map book.

clue.text: Booker Prize winner in demand before university called foul

indicators.note: something foul is spoiled or fouled up, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a hot item is much sought after
U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A popular prize-winning author shouting foul at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called foul' sounds like an accusation, but 'foul' is the signal to jumble the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel du Lac, Anita Brookner's novel, won the Booker Prize for fiction in 1984.

clue.text: Escort fuel once had this?

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: to guide someone inside
second meaning: petrol used to contain the metal as an additive

explanation.walkthrough: Escort looks like the Ford car, which leads you to fuel; in fact it is a verb, and the second half refers to leaded petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone in is to escort them inside; and until it was phased out, petrol contained added lead.

clue.text: Iron Duke not due to appear in high-class gathering after having gone downhill

indicators.note: not having something means it is taken away
to appear inside something is to be held within it

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with 1 read as I
to iron clothes is to press them
taken as written
taken as written
surface padding: the first-rate letters are read as a social gathering

explanation.surface: Wellington, the Iron Duke, skipping a smart society gathering after falling from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Duke is the Duke of Wellington, but the phrase splits in two. Après-ski is French, hence the accent missing from the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is French for 'after skiing', the socialising that follows a day on the slopes.

clue.text: Progressive increase of delight about regular social appearances

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: elation is great delight
first, third and fifth letters
surface padding: completes the idea of letters that appear regularly

explanation.surface: Someone's pleasure growing steadily as their party invitations become frequent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearances' completes the selection phrase: the letters that regularly appear from the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalation is a gradual, step-by-step rise in intensity or scale, as in a conflict or prices.

clue.text: Take time out to obtain closure

indicators.note: out means removed or excluded, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to take without permission is to steal
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Advice to pause and reflect in order to get emotional closure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take time out' is a familiar phrase for a break, but here it means remove T from a synonym of take.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is something that closes an opening tightly, such as on a jar or envelope.

clue.text: Seven from Paris quietly going for more time in subterranean home

indicators.note: one thing going in exchange for another means a swap

blocks.note: sept is French for seven
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Parisian group of seven going underground for longer.
explanation.walkthrough: In SEPT, the P is replaced by a T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the burrow system in which badgers live, an underground dwelling.

clue.text: Paris summit proscribed synthetic dress

indicators.note: the top being banned means the first letter is removed
synthetic means artificially made, so the letters are put together anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Paris fashion meeting banning garments made of artificial fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: PARIS loses its top letter to leave ARIS, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a long wrapped garment worn chiefly by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Conventional way of reaching country home kept by the French?

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it

blocks.note: a country is a land
le is French for the
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Asking the traditional route to a country house in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a road to the country, but 'reaching' means contacting someone by phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A landline is a fixed telephone connection, the traditional means of contacting someone before mobiles.

clue.text: Gold accepted by first person to get gold for acting great

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: me is the first person pronoun
or is gold in heraldry
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: The first performer ever to win a gold award for acting.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold is clued twice: OR, the heraldic word, inside ME, and then AU, the chemical symbol, added on.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeanne Moreau was a celebrated French film actress, a star of the New Wave cinema.
